title: The Ledger of the Cape Route
premise: In the port town of Vellermont, Marguerite Dravenmoor keeps her father's type foundry running while revolution brews in the capital. When the army requisitions the town, they seize the parish ledger holding every name, debt, and secret of its people — and Marguerite, who once cut the very type that printed it, is conscripted to forge a sanitized replacement. Instead she begins secretly resetting the true record, hiding names inside decorative flourishes and marginalia, aided by a young officer, Captain Aurel Sennet, who must choose between his uniform and his conscience. As the victors' historians arrive to burn the original ledger, Marguerite prints one clandestine true edition and smuggles it aboard a ship on the Cape Route; she loses her father's shop and nearly her life, but the truth survives at sea, and years later it returns to rebuild the town's memory — with her name finally in it.
about_author: Mirabel Vasquez is a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring printing archives along old colonial trade routes before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal studio where a nineteenth-century hand press still occupies half the room.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sorts
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. On the eve of unrest, she measures her world in what can be carried: lead type, her father's failing eyesight, a courtship she keeps postponing. When news arrives that the army will requisition Vellermont, the townsfolk look to the ledger as proof of who they are. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath ordinary tenderness, the calm before confiscation.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, with interludes from Captain Sennet's journal. Soldiers seize the parish ledger; Marguerite is ordered to cut new type for an 'official' version that erases debts, deaths, and dissent. She recognizes Sennet as a boy she once taught letters to. Emotional beat: humiliation curdling into resolve — she agrees to comply while planning her forgery of truth.

chapters.title: Names Hidden in Flourishes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Marguerite and Sennet. By candlelight she embeds the real names into ornamental borders only a compositor could read; Sennet discovers her work and, torn between duty and love, becomes her lookout. The historians' arrival date moves up. Emotional beat: intimacy forged in shared risk, love sharpened by the knowledge that betrayal or sacrifice is coming.

chapters.title: The Cape Route
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, closing with Sennet's final journal entry. During the burning of the original ledger, she triggers a diversion, pulls the true plates, and races to the harbor as the town burns behind her. Wounded, she watches the ship clear the cape carrying the hidden edition. Epilogue: years later, the book returns and the names are read aloud. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into permanence — survival priced, but truth paid forward.
